PSALM LXVI. 
 
  The psalmist calls on all people to praise God, for his sovereign   power over the whole creation, ver. 1-7.   For his special favour to his people, ver. 8-12.   Praises him for his goodness to himself in particular, ver. 13-20.   To the chief musician, A song or psalm. 
 
  V. 1. All lands-Ye people of all nations.  He invites the Gentile world, to the contemplation and celebration of God's works.
V. 6. We-Our nation, or our ancestors, in whose loins we then were.
V. 10. Proved us-As it were in a burning furnace; and with a design to purge out our dross.
V. 11. Net-Which our enemies laid for us.
V. 12. To ride-To use us like slaves.
V. 15. I will go-One speaks in the name of all the rest. Incense-With the fat of rams, which is no less pleasing to God than incense.

V. 18. Iniquity-Any sin.  In heart-If my heart had been false to God, although I might have forborne outward acts.  If I had been guilty of that, by heart was set upon sin, or I desired only that which I resolved in my heart to spend upon my lusts.
